title.narrative: UNDP: Stöd till RC/HC:s kontor Damaskus
UNDP: Support to RC/HC Office Damascus

description.narrative: FNs samordning kontor i Damaskus (kontor för RC/HC) fyller en viktig funktion för koordinering av insatser och mobiisering av resurser. Ambassaden har fått en förfrågan och beslutat om ett ettårigt stöd för att stärka kontorets kapacitet genom att finansiera två tjänster. Inriktningen för den ena tjänsten är att stödja arbetet med de humanitära principerna för skydd till befolkningen och policyarbete för att stärka mänskliga rättigheterna i landet (Senior Policy Advisor). Den andra tjänsten omfattar strategisk planering och programmering av humanitära/fredsinsatser samt stöd till förbättrade riskanalyser och riskhantering. (Strategic Planning and coordination Speciaist). UNDP är Sidas avtalspartner. Jämställdhet är ett viktigt mål för både experter. Insatsen förändrades i januari 2020: stöd till kommunikation expert hos ORCHC under 2020, sedan i juni 2020: stöd till risk hantering enheten.

The Office of the UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Syria (RC/HC) plays an important role in coordinating the humanitarian operations and mobilising resources in Syria. The Embassy Ambassaden har received a request and decided on a one year support to strenghten the capacity of the office, by financing two positions. One position is a Senior Policy Advisor that will work with humanitarian protection, human rights policy and advocacy and the other positions is a Strategic Planning and Coordination Specialist working with strategic programming and planning of humanitarian development/peace nexus issues, risk analysis and risk management. UNDP is the agreement partner.
The two experts will work on advocacy and strategic planning for the whole aid community in Syria, including the definition of the UN joint programme and for the humanitarian response plan. Ensuring that girls and women are not discriminated from humanitarian assistance, protection and planning of resilience interventions is one of the objective of the work of the experts at the office of the RC/HC in Damascus, therefore gender qualifies as a significant policy.
The ORCHC could obtain visa for the IHL expert. The support has been partly use to support the Strategic planning specialist in 2018-2019. The contribution agreement has been amended in June 2020 to incluse instead a 9 month support to the ORCHC's Communication officer and the a 12 month support to the newly established risk management unit, both serving the UN Country Team and the Humanitarian Country Team as well.

The overarching objective of the intervention is to strengthen the Resident Coordinator's Office (RCO) in Damascus capacity to manage the significant risks associated with UN operations inside Syria. Syria is a uniquely complicated operating environment, with significant risks for aid diversion, corruption, and instrumentalization. Moreover, it is of the highest priority that international sanctions are respected and that no aid funding ends up with the regime. Sida's partnership with the RCO is a concerted effort to improve coordination and knowledge of these topics within the Damascene UN system.
Through the establishment of a dedicated Risk Management Unit (RMU) within the RCO, the intervention aims to bolster the UN's ability to effectively identify, assess and mitigate risks associate with its operations in Syria, ultimately ensuring the safety and success of its activities in the region.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Under a Third-Party Cost Sharing Agreement signed in June 2018 between the Government of Sweden and UNDP, Swedish funds were initially provided to support strategic staffing in the Resident Coordinators Office (RCO) and OCHA. However, following the 2019 restructuring of the RCO as part of the UN Secretary-Generals reforms, these functions became part of the globally standardized core staffing, requiring an amendment to the agreement.
Subsequently, after consultations between the UN RC/HC and the Embassy of Sweden, it was agreed to repurpose the remaining funds to enhance the UNs risk management capacity in Syria through the establishment of a dedicated Risk Management Unit (RMU) within the RCO in Damascus.
Operating in one of the worlds most complex and dynamic environments, marked by significant uncertainty, the UN in Syria has had to navigate a wide spectrum of operational and programmatic risks. To strengthen accountability and improve inter-agency coordination in this high-risk context, the RMU was established as a strategic response mechanism.
Swedens contribution enabled the establishment and subsequent expansion of the RMU within the RCO in Damascus, where it became operational in mid-2021. The RMU has since served as a centralized hub for promoting coherent risk management approaches and unified methodologies across UN agencies operating in Syria.
The RCO have compiled the below timeline of results and activities conducted by the RMU during the projects lifetime:
2021: Operationalization and Strategic Coordination
The RMU became fully operational within the RCO in Damascus:
1. A national Risk Register was launched, identifying 14 priority risks and outlining 72 mitigation measures.
2. Advisory notes were produced to guide UN agencies in risk-informed planning.
3. Internal coordination mechanisms were activated to support consistent risk engagement across UN agencies.
4. The RMU began supporting donor coordination through the Regional Dialogue Mechanism.
2022: Strengthening Risk Systems and Tools
Key systems and guidance materials were developed to standardize risk practices:
1. The Risk Management Guide was updated to reflect evolving operational contexts and best practices.
2. A Watch List mechanism was introduced to monitor emerging and context-specific risks.
3. Donor coordination was strengthened, particularly through the Regional Dialogue Mechanism.
4. The CRR was updated quarterly, with enhanced monitoring and due diligence guidance shared across agencies.
5. Risk monitoring mechanisms were piloted to build operational accountability.
2023: Integration into Crisis Response and Strategic Expansion
The RMU adapted to real-time challenges and advanced system-wide coherence:
1. A Crisis Risk Log was developed and used during the Syria earthquake response, enabling timely risk tracking.
2. The RMU led inter-agency efforts on Implementing Partner (IP) salary harmonization and conducted procurement risk analyses.
3. Drafting of SOPs and risk assessment forms standardized operational risk approaches.
4. A concept note was developed for scaling up the RMU model for broader impact across the UN system.
2024: Institutionalization and Transition to Sustainability
The RMU enhanced existing tools in accordance with international best practices and developed supplementary risk instruments to address evolving operational demands. With core systems firmly established, the unit advanced its transition toward long-term institutional integration within the UN framework:
1. The RMU led the Programme Criticality Assessment (PCA) in collaboration with the Programme Management Team (PMT) and the UN Country Team (UNCT).
2. Established SOPs for Enterprise Risk Management and institutionalized the UNCT Risk Update to enhance strategic risk oversight.
3. A Risk Appetite Statement was launched, providing strategic alignment for UNCT decision-making.
4. Risk communication strategies were embedded into UNCT messaging and planning processes.
5. Facilitated the RMWG to advance coordination and implement core risk tools.
6. Strengthened collaboration with thematic working groups such as AAP, HACT, CWG, and PWG, particularly in their risk identification and work planning processes.
7. Final coordination with donors was completed, and a sustainability proposal was submitted to ensure long-term risk governance beyond the life of the project.
Taken together, the RMU has contributed to the following overarching results:
Key results achieved:
a. Institutionalized risk management practices across the UN Syria coordination system.
b. Developed and operationalized tools and frameworks that standardize risk analysis and mitigation.
c. Fostered a culture of inter-agency collaboration, strengthening risk accountability and transparency.
d. Created pathways for evidence-based decision-making through systematic risk reporting (e.g., Risk Updates).e.
e. Increased visibility and strategic relevance of risk management in UN Syria operations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
